explanation.text: The Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties entered into force on January 27, 1980, according to the official record from the United Nations Treaty Collection.
Article 84(1) of the Vienna Convention specifies the conditions for its entry into force, which were met on January 27, 1980.
The United Nations Treaty Collection, a primary and authoritative source, confirms the entry into force date as January 27, 1980.
Wikipedia corroborates that the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties became effective on January 27, 1980.
The ratification status and effective date in the Wikipedia entry align with the official United Nations record.

excerpts.text: The Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties was adopted and opened to signature on 23 May 1969,[[6]](#cite_note-Law_of_treaties-6)[[1]](#cite_note-untreaty-1-1) became effective on 27 January 1980,[[1]](#cite_note-untreaty-1-1) and has been ratified by 119 sovereign states as of May 2026.[[2]](#cite_note-rat-2) Non-ratifying parties, such as the U.S., have recognized parts of the VCLT as a restatement of [customary international law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Customary_international_law "Customary international law").[[7]](#cite_note-Is_the_United_States_a_party_to_the_Vienna_Convention_on_the_Law_of_Treaties?-7) In treaty law, the VCLT is the authority for resolving disputes about the [interpretation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judicial_interpretation "Judicial interpretation") of a treaty.[[8]](#cite_note-juridicum.univie.ac.at-8)
